results.title: Modem Reboot Procedure
results.snippet: Reboot the modem when the customer reports: - No internet connection despite modem appearing powered on - Very slow speeds that did not improve after router restart

results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

results.title: Device Compatibility — Approved Modems and Routers
results.snippet: Customers must use a modem on the ISP-approved list to receive full technical support. Unapproved modems may work but are not guaranteed to provision correctly or receive remote management commands (including `reboot_modem_remotely`).

<analysis>
I've gathered the following diagnostic evidence:

**Customer Profile** [tool:lookup_customer]: Jane Smith, active account since 2021, Gigabit 500 service tier, NETGEAR CM500 modem in the northeast (ZIP 10001).

**Modem Status** [tool:check_modem_status]: The modem is technically online but showing severe problems:
- Downstream signal at -12 dBmV (well outside acceptable range; should be between -7 and +7 dBmV per KB)
- Upstream signal at 44 dBmV (also elevated)
- Signal quality marked as "weak"
- 7 restarts in the last 24 hours (indicating instability)
- Uptime only 0.5 hours (modem just restarted)
- Firmware note flags "line issue"

**Connectivity Test** [tool:ping_customer_modem]: High latency (287 ms) and 12.5% packet loss—consistent with a signal/line problem.

**Outage Check** [tool:check_isp_outage]: No active ISP outages in the customer's area.

**KB Findings** [kb:slow_speeds]: Weak downstream signal (below -7 dBmV) indicates a line-level issue, not a WiFi or congestion problem.

**Diagnosis**: This is a **line-quality issue** at the ISP side (poor signal from the cable plant to the modem), not a customer-side WiFi problem or outage. The orange lights, frequent restarts, and weak signal all point to the modem struggling to maintain a stable connection due to degraded incoming signal. This requires a technician visit to inspect the line.
</analysis>

<reply>
I can see what's happening here. Your modem is showing a weak signal coming in from our network—that's why you're seeing those orange lights and it keeps restarting. This isn't something a reboot will fix; it's a line issue on our end that needs a technician to come out and check the cable connection to your house. Let me get you scheduled for a visit as soon as possible.
</reply>
